Petrol is a mixture of hydrocarbons (mainly carbon and hydrogen compounds such as C₄–C₁₂).
Ethanol has the chemical formula C₂H₅OH.
Why ethanol absorbs water:
Ethanol contains a hydroxyl (-OH) group, which is polar.
Water (H₂O) is also polar.
The -OH group forms hydrogen bonds with water, so ethanol readily absorbs moisture from the air (it is hygroscopic).
How ethanol can damage an engine (if water contamination becomes significant):
Water can separate from the petrol-ethanol mixture (phase separation).
The engine may receive a water-rich fuel layer, causing hard starting, misfiring, corrosion, and rust.
Water also reduces lubrication in some fuel-system components and can damage injectors or fuel pumps over time.

Water consumption: Sugarcane, India's primary ethanol feedstock, is a water-intensive crop. Expanding sugarcane cultivation in water-stressed states can put additional pressure on groundwater and rivers.
Food vs. fuel: Diverting sugarcane juice or maize to ethanol production may compete with food production or influence agricultural markets, although the government also uses surplus sugar and damaged grains in some cases.
Lower fuel efficiency: Ethanol contains about one-third less energy per litre than petrol, so higher ethanol blends generally reduce mileage.
Questionable climate benefits: The overall greenhouse gas benefit depends on how the feedstock is grown, irrigation, fertilizer use, transportation, and processing. If these are carbon-intensive, the environmental advantage can be much smaller.
Air pollution: Ethanol can reduce some emissions, such as carbon monoxide, but it may increase others under certain conditions, depending on the engine and emission controls. Air-quality effects are not uniformly positive.
Vehicle compatibility: Older vehicles and some motorcycles not designed for higher ethanol blends may experience material degradation or fuel-system issues.
